title: Q-CTRL Raises $290 Million in Series C Funding Led by Salesforce Ventures to Scale Quantum Infrastructure Software - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Q-CTRL raised an oversubscribed US$290M Series C led by Salesforce Ventures at a valuation above $1B, described as the largest private raise for a software-focused quantum firm. New backers include AMD Ventures, EDGE Group and Australia's NRFC; funds go to AI-driven control software, quantum navigation, and Japan expansion.

insights.claim: Q-CTRL secured US$290 million (A$415 million) in an oversubscribed Series C led by Salesforce Ventures, valuing the company above $1 billion.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A unicorn valuation for a quantum software firm marks investor appetite for the picks-and-shovels layer of quantum.

insights.claim: Q-CTRL's Series C was expanded twice to accommodate institutional demand and is described as the largest private capital raise recorded for a software-focused quantum technology firm.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Oversubscription signals strong private-market demand for quantum exposure in late 2026.
insights.quote: represents the largest private capital raise recorded for a software-focused quantum technology firm

insights.claim: Q-CTRL's Series C follows a $113M Series B in October 2024 and a $27.4M Series B-1 in January 2023.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Round sizes have scaled sharply, about 2.6x from Series B to C.

insights.claim: New Q-CTRL backers include AMD Ventures, EDGE Group, Australia's NRFC, MPower Partners and SPARX Asset Management, strengthening ties across semiconductors, defense and Japanese industrial markets.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Sovereign and defense capital in the round reflects quantum's strategic and national-security framing.

insights.claim: Returning Q-CTRL investors include Lockheed Martin Ventures, In-Q-Tel, DCVC, Main Sequence and Square Peg, alongside Bullhound Capital and Affinity Partners as anchor investors.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Continued defense and intelligence-linked backing points to government demand for quantum sensing and navigation.

insights.claim: Q-CTRL's products include Fire Opal and Boulder Opal, which suppress noise and automate calibration in gate-model quantum computers, and Ironstone Opal for GPS-denied quantum magnetic navigation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Q-CTRL has a hardware-agnostic computing business plus a nearer-term defense sensing product, diversifying revenue.

insights.claim: Ironstone Opal has achieved RTCA DO-160 airworthiness qualification across commercial aviation and unmanned platforms, and Q-CTRL's Fire Opal Dynamics Simulator is deployed in the IBM Quantum Functions Catalog.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Airworthiness qualification is a concrete step toward commercial revenue from quantum navigation.

insights.claim: Q-CTRL plans to use the capital to expand its AI-driven control software stack, scale deployments across finance, energy, defense and aerospace, and accelerate expansion into Japan's industrial and high-performance computing sectors.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Japan and defense/aerospace are the stated growth vectors to watch.
